title: King Oliver's band in San Francisco and Clem's Balcony Ballroom band
summary: Hearing Oliver's band on Market Street, Clem's own travelling work and eleven-piece band, and the tune King Porter Stomp.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: When did you hear Oliver play that? Before you left New Orleans?
Oh, no. He came out here with the band.
You know he was in San Francisco over there on Market Street. He came from Chicago here.
Yeah, I showed fast where that was. What was it?
Pergola. It's a big market there now, I think.
Right about next to St. Francis Theater.
Do you remember Oliver and out here, too? You got to know him and hear the band when they were here?
Were you up in San Francisco over that time or down there?

I'd go all over. I always had a car and that's how I used to make my living. I'd go up this far to Portland, Oregon. Just play around, play around and come back down. Then for about nine months, I worked on Market Street. I don't remember the years. It was the Balcony Ballroom when I had 11 pieces over there. So Oliver was out here and that's the time Dodge was with him. They had the drummer Ram. He's still around here somewhere.
I talked to him on the phone in Los Angeles.
He did. In Minor Hall. They call him Ram.
We'll see him when we get back.

Oh, I see. He stood and the rest of the guys went by. That's one of the great numbers. I just thought it was King Oliver's number and they had music to it. So somebody put it down in music. But when Jelly Roll was playing it in Los Angeles, there wasn't no music to it.
Did you all play the Pearls too?
Yeah, that's his. That's one of his. I know that.
